findings.state: Any open deal whose top-ranked risk factor is the champion or economic-buyer rule while that field holds a short name. Rendered in today's SMB walkthrough, state 'After clicking ‹' (Sweetgreen, Negotiation): the 'What usually happens next' paragraph, the copied risk summary, and the previous/oldest screens' second sheet.
findings.current: "No champion is recorded. In negotiation, deals without someone inside defending the business case often stall in procurement when pushback comes. Find who will fight for this internally before the next approval round." — shown on the same screen as CHAMPION "Rafael Ibanez" and ECONOMIC BUYER "Whitney Cole". The same hard-coded opener is at autopsy-data.ts:123 (discovery), and "No economic buyer is recorded." opens the leads at :129 and :131.
findings.problem: The sentence is false. stageLead() returns these leads whenever the top risk factor is no_champion / no_eb, and those rules fire when the field is empty OR shorter than 20 characters (vitals.ts:88-93 gate(); causes.ts:36 and :48 use v.missing.*, which is true for 'weak'). A person's name is almost always shorter than 20 characters, so a deal with a named champion is told 'No champion is recorded' and 'Find who will fight for this internally' directly under a row that shows the champion's name. Node probe confirms the same for the economic buyer in negotiation and pilot stages ('No economic buyer is recorded…' with economicBuyer = 'Whitney Cole'). A first-time user is misled about their own record, and the false line travels into 'Copy risk summary' (the text a seller pastes into email or Slack). The literal rewrite created this: the old line ('No real champion carried this inside') was a judgment; the new one is a factual claim that the code does not check.

findings.problem: The day count reads as a forecast, but it is a display rule: 90 minus the risk score, limited to 7–90 days and shortened to the close date (autopsy.ts:44-60; the code comment says it 'is not a prediction that the deal will be lost on that date'). The reader cannot tell what the number means or how certain it is (the brief's first three questions; dimension 4 and dimension 2). The headline form itself is owner-approved (CLAUDE.md §4.14 and session log 2026-07-10) and is not in question.
